ruling.recommended_action: Uphold the $16.17 fare; close the dispute as not upheld and inform the rider that the 1.4x surge notice was validly served before pickup, so the surge-increased fare stands.
ruling.reasoning:
Dispute type is fare (surge), not route deviation: the GPS/fare records show actual distance 3.9 km against optimal 3.9 km (+0.0 km) [F1][F3], so no RD refund arises (deviation ≤ 1 km, RD-1). The whole $3.46 gap between the $12.71 quote [F6] and the $16.17 charged [F5] is attributable to surge rising from 1× to 1.4× [F8], so this is decided under SURGE-1/SURGE-2/SURGE-3.

The required notice: the surge log shows an in-app message at 17:18:45, before trip start at 17:20:00 [F9], stating the new multiplier ("Fares are 1.4× higher right now"), the revised estimated fare ("Your new estimated fare is $17.29") and a free-cancel option ("You can cancel for free"). All three SURGE-1 items are present, so the rider was notified; the notice precedes the trip, so SURGE-1's timing requirement is met. Under SURGE-2 (surge rose, rider notified, rider rode) the outcome is no_action — the higher fare stands — and no surge differential is refundable.

Even if one argued the fare-differential path, the arithmetic does not support the claimed $3.46: the surge component is (1.4 − 1) × $10.66 = $4.26, capped at the $3.46 the fare exceeds the quote [F8], and the rider's own $3.46 figure is not the correct measure of an unwarranted overcharge in any event. The rider's request for the full $3.46 difference therefore fails.

Profile facts were considered but never decide: the rider's single fraud flag [F14] only raises the confidence threshold to 95% under TH-3; the only judgment that turns on a text is the surge notice, which is complete and contradicts the rider's claim of no notice. Evidence (fare breakdown, surge log with timestamp, GPS, timestamped chats) is complete, so confidence exceeds the raised threshold. The driver's after-the-fact statement [F13] adds nothing and is not relied on.

element_findings.element: Surge notice stated the new multiplier (SURGE-1)
element_findings.reason: In-app notice at 17:18:45 (before 17:20:00 start) says 'Fares are 1.4× higher right now' — the new multiplier is stated.

element_findings.element: Surge notice stated the revised estimated fare (SURGE-1)
element_findings.reason: Notice says 'Your new estimated fare is $17.29', a revised estimate.
Notice says 'You can cancel for free' — an express no-penalty cancellation statement, unlike a mere 'fees may apply'.

element_findings.element: Notice served before or at pickup (SURGE-1/RD-5 timing)
element_findings.reason: Logged at 17:18:45, before the 17:20 pickup/trip start.

rejected_claims.reason: Chat #1 and #2 concern only the pickup arrangement (kerb location, arriving car); they contain no route or fare agreement and do not bear on the surge notice.
Driver's post-trip statement is a claim, not evidence of consent or notice; it is not relied on and is contradicted by no system record.
The 1.4x multiplier and charged fare are correct as built up; they do not show an overcharge once the valid pre-trip notice is established.
